title: Side Length and Area of a Square as Functions of Diagonal Length
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Write the side length s of a square as a function of the length d of the square's diagonal. Then write the area A of the square as a function of the diagonal length d.

steps.title: Relate Side Length s and Diagonal d via the Pythagorean Theorem
steps.explanation: A diagonal of length d divides a square of side length s into two congruent isosceles right triangles with legs of length s and hypotenuse d.
steps.why: The interior angles of a square are right angles, so the sides and diagonal satisfy the Pythagorean theorem.

steps.title: Solve for the Side Length s(d)
steps.explanation: Divide both sides of 2s^2 = d^2 by 2 and take the positive square root (since lengths are positive) to get s(d) = d / sqrt(2).
steps.why: Geometric lengths are positive quantities, selecting the principal square root.

steps.title: Express the Area A as a Function of d
steps.explanation: Since the area of a square is A = s^2 and 2s^2 = d^2, substituting s = d / sqrt(2) yields A(d) = d^2 / 2.
steps.why: Squaring s(d) eliminates the radical and expresses the area directly in terms of d.
